headline: Highest risk is data leakage and capability conflict: a local filesystem-writing, shell-executing content agent can mishandle secrets and outputs when paired with a docs-only LangChain4j wrapper.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between langchain4j and the course agent, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, production-agentic-rag-course reads and writes files and processes stdin/stdout, while langchain4j is a general LLM orchestration library that could be used to pass untrusted text. The pathway is plausible but undocumented, so I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by copy-paste, files, or stdout/stderr text flow
IF production-agentic-rag-course treats langchain4j-generated text as instructions without filtering
mitigations: Add a one-line provenance label to every handoff
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text
Review any file or stdout bridge before enabling it
Use a fixed prompt template with explicit delimiters

B_data_leakage.rationale: production-agentic-rag-course explicitly handles configuration secrets and writes files, while langchain4j is a general framework with no stated isolation or secret-handling controls. Even though langchain4j has no network egress, the pair can still expose secrets through shared files, logs, or notebook artifacts in default local-development use. The interaction is plausible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF secrets from production-agentic-rag-course are written into files or notebooks accessible to langchain4j
IF langchain4j outputs are logged alongside configuration secrets
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared files
Rotate exposed API keys after any test run
Mask secrets in logs and notebook outputs
Restrict file permissions on the workspace
Separate secret-bearing runs from documentation runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: production-agentic-rag-course can execute shells, install packages, spawn subprocesses, read and write the filesystem, while langchain4j is a library layer with no stated locking or concurrency controls. The profiles do not show shared mutable state, but the overlap on local files and subprocess-driven workflows creates a realistic write-conflict path in default development setups. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory
IF either agent writes generated artifacts without file locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Add simple lock files around shared artifacts
Disable concurrent notebook and agent runs
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: production-agentic-rag-course includes agentic ask/stream endpoints and a LangGraph subagent model, so it can plausibly act on upstream text. langchain4j is an orchestration library that may generate or route outputs, but the profiles do not prove verification steps between them. Because the handoff could become authoritative without checks, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF langchain4j-produced text is fed into the course agent's ask or agentic-ask flow
IF the course agent executes downstream actions without human review
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking endpoint
Require citations for generated claims
Compare outputs against source documents before use
Log and review agent-to-agent handoffs
Disable autonomous action mode for production runs

E_compliance.rationale: production-agentic-rag-course explicitly touches configuration secrets and requests elevated privileges, while langchain4j is an open-source library with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. The pair therefore creates a compliance gap around secret handling and local-development logging, but there is no evidence of PHI or a specific residency mismatch. I rate this medium due to the documented secret exposure surface.
conditions: IF regulated or customer secrets are processed in the shared environment
IF logs or notebooks retain those secrets beyond the intended session
mitigations: Delete notebook outputs after each run
Rotate any secrets used in testing
Document retention limits for local artifacts
Keep regulated data out of the course environment
Use separate credentials for demos and production
